questions.note: Height, stance width, shoulder line and arm lengths land on the reference in the onion. The head reads wider and squarer with a tall hair crest; the legs read thin and long (beyond the declared thigh length) because the trousers are narrow tubes; the feet look small in low boots.

Stance, lean, elbow positions and the carbine's diagonal follow the reference well. The outline is much leaner: no trouser bagginess, no blousing at the boots, slimmer forearms and gloves, shorter boots, the right pauldron higher and further out than drawn, and a spiked hair outline.

Gaiter, carrier, antenna, pauldrons, forearm guards, hip pouches and thigh rig are all present and near their places. But the left upper-arm plates stop well short of the drawn ones, the carrier front is three identical pouches rather than the drawn mix, the knee pads are plain boxes, and the boots are low trainers, not tall laced combat boots.

The order of layers is right and most kit rests on the body. The left hand lies open on the handguard instead of closing, the hems hang clear of the boots with a thin ankle showing, the shirt is painted on the muscles, a skin-coloured patch shows at the left shoulder, and the knee pads stand proud as slabs.

The reference is a bulky, heavily layered figure: baggy trousers, thick gloves, deep pouches, wide armour. The render is an athletic body in a tight suit with thin plates on it. Kit and cloth volume are well under the reference's everywhere below the carrier and on the arms.

The carbine's line and height against the body are right, allowing the declared real gun. The left hand does not grip: its fingers lie flat over the top of the handguard, where the reference wraps it from below. The right hand reads as laid on the receiver side with little sign of a closed grip. The gloves are thin bare-hand shapes.

defects.what: The face is not the reference man: wider and flatter, square forehead with a straight low hairline, heavy dark brow bar, small close-set eyes, short blunt nose, weak cheekbones and jaw definition, saturated orange skin.
defects.fix: The reference has a longer, narrower face, a higher M-shaped hairline, arched separate brows, deeper-set larger eyes, a longer straight nose, hollow cheeks and a tanned but neutral skin tone.

defects.what: The hair stands in a tall spiked crest that leaves the top of the frame, like a mohawk, with dense dark sides; the reference is a short textured crop about 30 mm high with a faded side.
defects.fix: Shorten the crown strands to a few centimetres, lay them forward and sideways in clumps, and fade the sides to stubble length.

defects.what: The left hand rests open on top of the handguard with straight fingers pointing down the far side; it does not close on the carbine. The reference wraps the handguard from below with curled fingers and the thumb over.
defects.fix: Bring the palm under the handguard and curl all four fingers round it, thumb along the near side.

defects.what: The boots read as low, smooth trainers: short shaft, thin pointed toe, slim sole, pale grey panels. The reference has tall laced combat boots with a bulbous toe cap, deep lugged sole, heel block and dark scuffed leather.
defects.fix: Raise the shaft to mid-shin height under the trouser, deepen the toe box and the sole, darken the upper to near black.

defects.what: The lower trousers are smooth narrow tubes ending in a straight hem above the boot; the reference trousers are baggy, with reinforced shin panels, stacked folds and the cuffs bloused over the boot tops.
defects.fix: Add cloth volume below the knee, the lighter shin reinforcement panels, and gather the hem onto the boot collar.

defects.what: The right hand is a thin bare-hand shape in a glove colour, lying against the receiver with no visible wrap of a pistol grip; the reference glove is bulky, with knuckle padding and a broad cuff under the forearm guard.
defects.fix: Close the lower three fingers round the grip with the web high on the backstrap, and give the glove its padded thickness.

defects.what: The arm armour is a clean light grey, far lighter than the reference (white in the diff): the drawn plates are dark gunmetal with tan worn edges and olive-brown grime, close in value to the shirt.
defects.fix: Drop the plates' base value by about half and warm it; keep bright values only on worn edges.

defects.what: The carrier is a flat grey-olive with three identical smooth pouches and a plain chest panel; the reference carrier is a warmer coyote-olive, heavily worn, with a detailed chest panel and unequal flapped pouches.
defects.fix: Shift the carrier hue toward yellow-olive, raise saturation, and vary the pouch row as drawn.

defects.what: A skin-coloured orange-brown patch shows at the left shoulder beside the carrier strap, below the antenna, where there should be only shirt and strap.
defects.fix: Find what is showing through (the body through the shirt, or an unassigned material) and cover or correct it.

defects.what: The left upper-arm armour ends about a third of the way up from the elbow, leaving a long bare sleeve; the reference stacks a pauldron and a long second plate with an olive band that reach nearly to the elbow.
defects.fix: Lengthen the lower plate and add the olive wrap so the armour covers the upper arm as drawn.

defects.what: The knee pads are plain rounded boxes with a raised hexagon, standing proud of the leg; the reference pads have a faceted shield-shaped cap in a tan frame with side wings, seated on a dark padded backing.
defects.fix: Shape the cap as a tapering faceted shield, add the frame and wings, and seat it into the backing.

defects.what: The shirt follows every muscle of the back and upper arms like paint; the reference shirt is a loose combat shirt with seams, sleeve folds and its own thickness.
defects.fix: Give the shirt ease over the shoulders and arms so it bridges the muscle forms and folds at the elbow and armpit.

defects.what: The right thigh rig's two cases have bright tan faces on black bodies; in the reference the cases are dark grey-black with only faint tan wear, and read as one dark mass.
defects.fix: Darken the case faces to near the body colour and keep tan for worn edges only.

ranked: [D1] The face is another man: broad, flat and square with a heavy brow bar, small eyes and orange skin, where the reference has a long lean face, high hairline, arched brows and hollow cheeks. Identity fails at a glance.
The whole figure reads as an athlete in a tight suit with plates attached, not the reference's bulky layered soldier. The mass of cloth and kit is well under the drawing on the arms, hips and legs.
[D3] The left hand lies open over the handguard and does not hold the carbine; the reference grips from below with closed fingers.
[D4] The boots are low pale trainers with pointed toes; the reference has tall, dark, heavy laced combat boots with deep lugged soles.
[D5] The trousers below the knee are narrow smooth tubes with a straight hem and a thin ankle showing; the reference is baggy, panelled and bloused over the boots.
[D2] The hair is a tall spiked crest that runs out of the frame; the reference is a short textured crop with faded sides.
[D7] The arm armour is light clean grey; the reference plates are dark gunmetal with tan worn edges, near the shirt in value. The diff map is white across every plate.
[D8] The carrier is too grey and too tidy: three identical pouches and a plain panel, against a warm worn olive carrier with unequal flapped pouches.
[D6] The right hand does not read as closed on a pistol grip, and both gloves are bare-hand shapes without padding or cuffs.
[D12] The shirt is skin-tight over the back, shoulders and arms; the reference shirt has ease, seams and folds.
[D10] The left upper-arm plates stop short and leave a long bare sleeve above the elbow; the drawn plates and olive band nearly reach the elbow.
[D11] The knee pads are plain boxes with a hexagon, proud of the leg; the drawn caps are faceted shields in a tan frame with side wings.
[D9] A skin-coloured patch shows at the left shoulder beside the strap, under the antenna.
The right pauldron sits higher and further outboard than drawn and is a single smooth plate; the reference has a smaller cap with a second plate under it running down the arm.
The gaiter is a tall smooth cowl of one value; the reference is a thinner scarf with deep irregular folds that sits lower on the neck and tucks inside the carrier straps.
The trouser cloth is a uniform brown-grey with soft blotches; the reference is darker, nearly black in the folds, with strong lighter wear on the thighs and shins.
[D13] The right thigh cases have bright tan faces; the drawn ones are dark throughout.
The emblem is a bright white star on mid blue; the reference is a duller pale crossed mark on a dark slate shield, less contrast and a different figure.

The carbine, though declared real, reads slim and toy-clean against the hands: a matte black with no wear and tan flecks only, where the drawn gun is worn grey metal with tan parts. Its value is too uniform.
